subject: maths
title: Addition and Subtraction Facts to 20
seo_title: Year 2 Addition and Subtraction Facts to 20 Worksheets: Bonds to 10, Doubles and Fact Families
standard_text: Recall and demonstrate proficiency with addition facts to 20; extend and apply facts to develop the related subtraction facts
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on addition and subtraction facts to 20: number bonds to 10 with ten frames, doubles, near doubles, make ten, fact families, missing numbers and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the Australian Curriculum.
key_big: Know your bonds to 10 and your doubles, and every fact to 20 gets easy.
body_html:
Start with number bonds to 10

Two numbers that make 10 are a number bond to 10. A ten frame shows them. Count the counters and the empty spaces.

Bond to 10Turned around
1 + 99 + 1
2 + 88 + 2
3 + 77 + 3
4 + 66 + 4
5 + 55 + 5

Three ways to add to 20

Doubles. 6 + 6 = 12, 7 + 7 = 14, 8 + 8 = 16, 9 + 9 = 18.

Near doubles. 7 + 8 is double 7 and 1 more: 14 + 1 = 15.

Make ten. Fill a ten frame first, then add the rest.

Example

What is 8 + 5?

8 needs 2 more to make 10. Take 2 from the 5. 3 is left. 10 + 3 = 13.

Answer: 13

Use addition to subtract

Three numbers make a fact family. If you know 8 + 5 = 13, you also know 13 − 5 = 8 and 13 − 8 = 5.

Example

What is 12 − 9?

Think: 9 + what = 12? Count up: 10, 11, 12. That is 3.

Answer: 3

Missing numbers

For 8 + ? = 15, count up from 8 to 15. Do not count the 8 you start on.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the start number: 9 + 4 = 12 (9, 10, 11, 12)Start on 9 and count the jumps: 10, 11, 12, 13
Mixing + and −: 14 − 6 = 20Read the sign first. Taking away gives a smaller number
7 + 8 = 147 + 7 = 14, so 7 + 8 is 1 more: 15
8 + ? = 15, so ? = 1515 is the total. Find the part: 15 − 8 = 7

faq.q: What addition facts should a Year 2 student know?
faq.a: The Australian Curriculum expects Year 2 students to recall addition facts to 20, such as 7 + 8 = 15, and use them to work out the related subtraction facts, such as 15 − 8 = 7.

faq.q: What are near doubles in maths?
faq.a: A near double is two numbers that are 1 apart, like 6 + 7. Use the double you know, 6 + 6 = 12, then add 1 to get 13.

faq.q: What is the make ten strategy?
faq.a: Move part of one number to make 10 first. For 9 + 4, move 1 to the 9 to make 10, then add the 3 left: 10 + 3 = 13.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn facts to 20 at home?
faq.a: Practise bonds to 10 with fingers or an egg carton, then doubles, for a few minutes every day. Ask “if 8 + 5 = 13, what is 13 − 5?” so your child links adding and subtracting.

sets.title: Number bonds to 10 with ten frames

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 7 counters and 3 empty spaces. 7 + 3 = 10, so 3 more make 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 4 counters and 6 empty spaces. 4 + 6 = 10, so 6 more make 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 9 counters and 1 empty space. 9 + 1 = 10, so 1 more makes 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 2 counters and 8 empty spaces. 2 + 8 = 10, so 8 more make 10.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: There are 6 counters and 4 empty spaces. 6 + 4 = 10, so 4 more make 10.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the ten frame?
items.e: There are 6 red counters and 4 blue counters. Together they fill the frame: 6 + 4 = 10.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the ten frame?
items.e: There are 3 red counters and 7 blue counters. Together they fill the frame: 3 + 7 = 10.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the ten frame?
items.e: There are 8 red counters and 2 blue counters. Together they fill the frame: 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: 3 counters are crossed out. What is 10 − 3?
items.e: Count the counters with no X. 10 − 3 = 7. Check: 7 + 3 = 10.

items.q: 6 counters are crossed out. What is 10 − 6?
items.e: Count the counters with no X. 10 − 6 = 4. Check: 4 + 6 = 10.

items.q: 8 counters are crossed out. What is 10 − 8?
items.e: Count the counters with no X. 10 − 8 = 2. Check: 2 + 8 = 10.

items.q: 1 counter is crossed out. What is 10 − 1?
items.e: Count the counters with no X. 10 − 1 = 9. Check: 9 + 1 = 10.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: The two parts make 10. 2 + 8 = 10, so the missing part is 8.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: The two parts make 10. 5 + 5 = 10, so the missing part is 5.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: The two parts make 10. 7 + 3 = 10, so the missing part is 3.

items.q: Which pair makes 10?
Which pair does NOT make 10?
items.e: 4 + 5 = 9, not 10. So 4 + 5 is not a number bond to 10.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 8 = 10
items.e: 2 + 8 = 10, so the missing number is 2. (18 adds instead: 10 + 8.)

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 1 = 10
items.e: 9 + 1 = 10, so the missing number is 9. (11 adds instead: 10 + 1.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 10 − ? = 4
items.e: Think: 4 + 6 = 10. So 10 − 6 = 4, and the missing number is 6.

sets.title: Facts to 20: doubles, near doubles and make ten

items.q: Each frame has 5 counters. What is 5 + 5?
items.e: This is a double. Double 5 is 10.

items.q: Each frame has 6 counters. What is 6 + 6?
items.e: This is a double. Double 6 is 12.

items.q: Each frame has 8 counters. What is 8 + 8?
items.e: This is a double. Double 8 is 16.

items.q: What is double 9?
items.e: Double 9 is 9 + 9. 9 + 9 = 18. (Think: 10 + 10 = 20, then take away 2.)

items.q: Use double 4. What is 4 + 5?
items.e: 4 + 5 is a near double. Double 4 is 8. 5 is 1 more than 4, so add 1: 9.

items.q: Double 6 and 1 more. What is 6 + 7?
items.e: 6 + 7 is a near double. Double 6 is 12. 7 is 1 more than 6, so add 1: 13.

items.q: Double 7 and 1 more. What is 7 + 8?
items.e: 7 + 8 is a near double. Double 7 is 14. 8 is 1 more than 7, so add 1: 15.

items.q: Use double 8. What is 8 + 9?
items.e: 8 + 9 is a near double. Double 8 is 16. 9 is 1 more than 8, so add 1: 17.

items.q: Which double helps you work out 6 + 7?
items.e: 7 is 1 more than 6. Double 6 is 12, then add 1: 13. So use 6 + 6, then add 1.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 9 + 4?
items.e: 9 needs 1 more to make 10. Take 1 from the 4: 3 is left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 8 + 5?
items.e: 8 needs 2 more to make 10. Take 2 from the 5: 3 is left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 9 + 7?
items.e: 9 needs 1 more to make 10. Take 1 from the 7: 6 is left. 10 + 6 = 16.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 8 + 6?
items.e: 8 needs 2 more to make 10. Take 2 from the 6: 4 is left. 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 7 + 5?
items.e: 7 needs 3 more to make 10. Take 3 from the 5: 2 is left. 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Make ten. 8 + 5 is the same as which?
items.e: Move 2 from the 5 to the 8. 8 + 2 = 10 and 3 is left. So 8 + 5 = 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Make ten. 9 + 6 is the same as which?
items.e: Move 1 from the 6 to the 9. 9 + 1 = 10 and 5 is left. So 9 + 6 = 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Start with the bigger number. What is 3 + 9?
items.e: Start at 9 and count on 3: 10, 11, 12. So 3 + 9 = 12. (11 counts the 9 as well.)

items.q: Make ten. What is 6 + 9?
items.e: Start with 9. Take 1 from the 6 to make 10. 5 is left. 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Make ten. What is 4 + 8?
items.e: Start with 8. Take 2 from the 4 to make 10. 2 is left. 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Kai says 7 + 8 = 14. What did he do wrong?
items.e: 7 + 7 = 14. But 8 is 1 more than 7, so 7 + 8 = 14 + 1 = 15. He did double 7 and forgot 1.

sets.title: Related subtraction facts and fact families

items.q: The frames show 8 + 5 = 13. Take away the blue counters. What is 13 − 5?
items.e: Take away the 5 blue counters. The 8 red counters are left. 13 − 5 = 8.

items.q: The frames show 9 + 6 = 15. Take away the blue counters. What is 15 − 6?
items.e: Take away the 6 blue counters. The 9 red counters are left. 15 − 6 = 9.

items.q: 7 + 5 = 12. Use this fact. What is 12 − 7?
items.e: If 7 + 5 = 12, then 12 − 7 = 5. Take away the red counters and the blue ones are left.

items.q: 8 + 6 = 14. Use this fact. What is 14 − 8?
items.e: If 8 + 6 = 14, then 14 − 8 = 6. Take away the red counters and the blue ones are left.

items.q: 6 + 5 = 11. Use this fact. What is 11 − 6?
items.e: If 6 + 5 = 11, then 11 − 6 = 5. Subtraction undoes addition.

items.q: 9 + 8 = 17. Use this fact. What is 17 − 9?
items.e: If 9 + 8 = 17, then 17 − 9 = 8. Subtraction undoes addition.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: Whole − part = the other part. 16 − 9 = 7. Check: 9 + 7 = 16.

items.q: What is the whole?
items.e: The whole is the two parts added: 7 + 6 = 13. (1 is 7 − 6.)

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: 14 − 8 = 6. Check: 6 + 8 = 14. (22 adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: Which subtraction matches the model?
items.e: Start with the whole and take away one part. The other part is left: 14 − 8 = 6.

items.q: Which addition matches the model?
items.e: Add the two parts to get the whole: 7 + 8 = 15. (7 + 8 is not 14. That is 7 + 7.)

items.q: Which fact is in the same family as 9 + 4 = 13?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers: 9, 4 and 13. 13 − 4 = 9 uses them all.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in the fact family for 6, 9 and 15?
items.e: 9 − 6 = 3 uses the number 3, not 15. The others use only 6, 9 and 15.

items.q: How many facts are in the fact family for 5, 8 and 13?
Which addition fact helps you work out 16 − 7?
Count up from 9 to 12. What is 12 − 9?
items.e: Think addition: 9 + 3 = 12. So 12 − 9 = 3.

items.q: Count up from 6 to 13. What is 13 − 6?
items.e: Think addition: 6 + 7 = 13. So 13 − 6 = 7.

items.q: Count up from 8 to 15. What is 15 − 8?
items.e: Think addition: 8 + 7 = 15. So 15 − 8 = 7.

items.q: Count up from 8 to 17. What is 17 − 8?
items.e: Think addition: 8 + 9 = 17. So 17 − 8 = 9.

items.q: Mia says 14 − 6 = 8. Which addition checks it?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away. 8 + 6 = 14, so Mia is right.

items.q: Find the missing number: 9 + ? = 12
items.e: Count up from 9 to 12: 10, 11, 12. That is 3 jumps, so the missing number is 3. (Do not count the 9 you start on.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 7 + ? = 11
items.e: Count up from 7 to 11: 8, 9, 10, 11. That is 4 jumps, so the missing number is 4. (Do not count the 7 you start on.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 8 + ? = 15
items.e: Count up from 8 to 15: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 7 jumps, so the missing number is 7. (Do not count the 8 you start on.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 6 + ? = 13
items.e: Count up from 6 to 13: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 7 jumps, so the missing number is 7. (Do not count the 6 you start on.)

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 5 = 12
items.e: Whole − part: 12 − 5 = 7. Check: 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 8 = 17
items.e: Whole − part: 17 − 8 = 9. Check: 9 + 8 = 17.

items.q: Find the missing number: 14 = 6 + ?
items.e: The = sign means both sides are the same. 6 + 8 = 14, so the missing number is 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: 15 − ? = 9
items.e: Count up from 9 to 15: that is 6. So 15 − 6 = 9, and the missing number is 6.

items.q: Find the missing number: 13 − ? = 5
items.e: Think: 5 + 8 = 13. So 13 − 8 = 5, and the missing number is 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? − 4 = 9
items.e: You took 4 away and 9 were left. Put the 4 back: 9 + 4 = 13. Check: 13 − 4 = 9. (5 takes away instead.)

items.q: Find the missing number: ? − 7 = 8
items.e: Put the 7 back: 8 + 7 = 15. Check: 15 − 7 = 8. (8 + 7 is not 14.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 20 − ? = 14
items.e: Count up from 14 to 20: that is 6. So the missing number is 6.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 6 = 20
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10, and 10 more makes 20. 4 + 10 = 14, so the missing number is 14. (4 only makes 10.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 11 + ? = 18
items.e: 1 + 7 = 8, so 11 + 7 = 18. The missing number is 7.

items.q: Find the missing number: 17 = ? + 9
items.e: Think: 9 + 8 = 17. So the missing number is 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: 12 = 20 − ?
items.e: Count up from 12 to 20: that is 8. So 20 − 8 = 12. The missing number is 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: 9 + 9 = ? + 10
items.e: 9 + 9 = 18. So ? + 10 must also be 18. 8 + 10 = 18, so the missing number is 8. (18 is only the left side.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 7 + 8 = 10 + ?
items.e: 7 + 8 = 15. So 10 + ? must also be 15. 10 + 5 = 15, so the missing number is 5. (4 comes from 7 + 8 = 14.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 6 + 7 = 7 + ?
items.e: You can add in any order. 6 + 7 = 7 + 6, so the missing number is 6.

items.q: Which number sentence is true?
Isla has 8 apples. She gets 5 more. How many apples does she have now?
items.e: Add. 8 + 2 = 10, then 3 more is 13. (12 counts the 8 as well.)

items.q: There are 9 students on the bus. 6 more get on. How many students are on the bus now?
items.e: Add. 9 + 1 = 10, then 5 more is 15.

items.q: Jack eats 7 grapes at recess. Mia eats 7 grapes too. How many grapes do they eat?
items.e: This is a double. 7 + 7 = 14.

items.q: Noah has 6 strawberries. Ava has 7 strawberries. How many strawberries do they have altogether?
items.e: Near double: double 6 is 12, and 1 more is 13.

items.q: There are 16 oranges in the fruit bowl. Year 2 eats 8 at recess. How many oranges are left?
4 koalas sit in one tree. 9 koalas sit in another tree. How many koalas are there?
items.e: Start with the bigger number: 9 + 1 = 10, then 3 more is 13.

items.q: There are 14 students on the bus. 6 get off. How many students are still on the bus?
items.e: Take away. 14 − 4 = 10, then take away 2 more: 8. (20 adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: 12 kookaburras sit on a fence. 5 fly away. How many kookaburras are left?
items.e: Take away. 12 − 2 = 10, then take away 3 more: 7.

items.q: Grace reads 9 pages on Monday and 9 pages on Tuesday. How many pages does she read?
items.e: This is a double. 9 + 9 = 18.

items.q: Our footy team kicks 6 goals, then 8 more goals. How many goals is that?
items.e: Near double: double 6 is 12, and 8 is 2 more than 6, so 12 + 2 = 14.

items.q: The canteen has 17 icy poles. It sells 9. How many icy poles are left?
items.e: Think addition: 9 + 8 = 17. So 17 − 9 = 8.

items.q: Ruby finds 18 shells at the beach. She gives 9 to her brother. How many shells does she have now?
items.e: Half of 18 is 9, because 9 + 9 = 18. So 18 − 9 = 9.

items.q: Leo has 15 footy cards. Kai has 9 footy cards. How many more cards does Leo have?
items.e: Find the difference. Count up from 9 to 15: that is 6. (24 adds them.)

items.q: The bus has 20 seats. 13 students sit down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Count up from 13 to 20: 13 + 7 = 20. So 7 seats are empty.

items.q: Some students are on the bus. 7 more get on. Now there are 16. How many were on the bus at first?
items.e: Take away the 7 that got on: 16 − 7 = 9. Check: 9 + 7 = 16.

items.q: Zara has 8 stickers. She gets some more. Now she has 15. How many stickers did she get?
items.e: Count up from 8 to 15: that is 7. Check: 8 + 7 = 15.

items.q: Cooper has $12. He spends $5 at the school fete. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Take away. $12 − $2 = $10, then take away $3 more: $7.

items.q: 13 students are in the pool at the swimming carnival. 5 get out. How many are still in the pool?
items.e: Take away. 13 − 3 = 10, then take away 2 more: 8.

items.q: There are 11 students on the bus. 4 get off. Then 6 get on. How many students are on the bus now?
items.e: Step 1: 11 − 4 = 7. Step 2: 7 + 6 = 13. (7 stops after step 1.)

items.q: Chloe has 7 apples. She buys 8 more. Which number sentence shows how many she has?
items.e: She gets more, so add. 7 + 8 is double 7 and 1 more: 7 + 8 = 15.
